newsitem.title: CROATIA: Tudjman drinks champagne after early lead in polls.
newsitem.headline: Tudjman drinks champagne after early lead in polls.

text.p: Croatian President Franjo Tudjman cracked a rare radiant smile and drank champagne on Sunday night as preliminary results for the presidential election gave him a clear lead over two opposition rivals.
First results, with some 57 percent of votes counted, showed Tudjman had won 59 percent, making sure he would not need to run off against an opposition candidate in the second round.
Dozens of HDZ supporters clapped their hands and chanted "Franjo, Franjo" but fell silent and looked amazed as a stunning fireworks display lit the warm night.

Before the results were announced, Tudjman's ruling Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ) laid a lavish banquet under a makeshift tent by the banks of the Sava river, with vintage wine, champagne and plenty of roast pork and lamb.

Shortly after Tudjman arrived, a group of teenage boys, waving Croatian and HDZ flags, flocked around him to the despair of his bodyguards, forcing the 75-year-old president to back off and jump on one of the tables to greet them.

He is now in a position to lead Croatia into the 21st century, as opponent Zdravko Tomac of the Social Democratic party got 22.8 percent of the votes counted and Vlado Gotovac of the Croatian Social Liberal Party 18.1 percent.
Tudjman has been hailed as the "father of the nation" since he proclaimed independence for Croatia after its secession from federal Yugoslavia in 1991.
"I told you before the election that my rivals would get half the votes that I get," a smiling Tudjman told state television reporters.
He has been reported to be suffering from cancer and unnamed U.S. officials said in November he had been treated for a form of stomach cancer in Washington.
But the former Yugoslav army general looked cheerful and energetic on Sunday and appeared to have gained some weight.
The crowd, singing 'There is only one Franjo Tudjman', started booing and laughing when a huge video screen showed the headquarters of the Social Democratic party.
"Franjo is with us, the reds are under our feet," they sang.
The media and HDZ often portrayed the Social Democrats as the successor to the Yugoslav communist party which ruled Croatia for 50 years.

Both opposition candidates, who made much of Tudjman's autocratic rule and lavish spending, complained they had not been treated equally by the state media. Their election night celebrations were subdued compared to Tudjman's, with no food, drink or jokes.
